Windows Phone 7 and the Metro interface

The 2010 phone operating system that introduced Metro by name, with a Start screen of flat colored live tiles.

Context

Windows Phone 7 was released worldwide on 21 October 2010 and in the United States on 8 November 2010. “It was designed with the distinct flat-style Metro interface.” (Wikipedia: Windows Phone 7).

The home screen, “Start screen”, is made up of live tiles that link to apps, contacts, and other items and update in real time. The default theme is dark; users can choose a light theme and an accent color, and tiles appear in that color.

Metro “was formally introduced as Metro during the unveiling of Windows Phone 7 in 2010”. Its designers cite transport signage as inspiration, and it uses Segoe fonts, including a Segoe WP family made for the phone (Wikipedia: Metro)).

The Industrial Designers Society of America gave Windows Phone 7 a Gold Interactive award, a People’s Choice award, and Best in Show at IDEA 2011 (Wikipedia: Metro)).

Why it belongs

The single-accent tile grid is the most compact statement of the style: content and type instead of chrome, and color as the only surface treatment.
